h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ז׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 7

p: At the end of Yoma (85b) it says:
'And I will sprinkle pure water upon you
and you shall be pure,' etc.
just as a mikveh purifies the tamei,
אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְטַהֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
so too Hakadosh Baruch Hu purifies Israel."
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא נז, א)
along the lines of our Sages' statement (Yoma 57a)
'Who dwells with them in the midst of their tumah.'"
And this is the verse said regarding Yom Kippur:
"And he shall atone for the Sanctuary," etc.,
"who dwells with them in the midst of their tumah";
"For on this day He shall atone for you
כִּי עִנְיַן הַשּׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם
For the meaning of "who dwells with them in the midst of their tumah"
is that the inner holiness of Israel
has not grown distant from the root of holiness;
עַל כָּל פָּנִים יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת אֶצְלָם
at any rate there can be among them
the dwelling and resting of holiness,
which is permitted while one's wife is tamei as a niddah.
"For on this day He shall atone for you
meaning that through the special virtue of this holy day
it brings about that the purity be complete,
so that there can be the union
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדַת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
And this is through the service of the Kohen Gadol
which is called "the chamber of the beds," as is known.
And to this the Gemara alludes:
meaning that the reason for their purity
is in order to be before Him, Yisbarach,
which is the ultimate aim of purity, as mentioned above.
"And Who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven" —
meaning that all matters of Israel's purity,
whether that there can be the resting of the Shechinah,
which is the matter of the first level,
or the ultimate aim of purity,
for completeness in union, as mentioned above,
come only from His power, Yisbarach.
And about this it goes on to explain,
"as it says, 'And I will sprinkle upon you
this is to establish the level
that He be "dwelling with them," etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And this is through the bestowal of words of Torah
into the heart of the souls of Israel,
as the plain sense of "I will sprinkle upon you":
like one who throws something on his fellow from afar.
is the bestowal of words of Torah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים
so that through this it will at any rate be
the foolish heart at one's left,
so as not to be lured.
that through words of Torah there comes about
לְהַכְנִיעוֹ לְפִי שָׁעָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים
subduing it at least for the time being,
and all this is from the help of Hashem Yisbarach,
אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֹזְרוֹ וְכוּ׳
"Were it not that Hakadosh Baruch Hu helps him," etc.
that there be at any rate
"And it says, 'The mikveh of Israel is Hashem':
just as a mikveh purifies the tamei,
אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְטַהֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
so too Hakadosh Baruch Hu purifies Israel" —
this refers to the second level,
which is the ultimate aim of purity,
for the completeness of union and joining.
And it is like the mikveh of water:
כִּי מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת ה׳
"For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem
as the waters cover the sea."
And daas means recognition and connection
as is known from the wording of the verse (Bereishis 4:1),
And the ultimate aim of purity was achieved
to be "before Hashem you shall be purified,"
And right after this comes the mitzvah of sukkah,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּחוּד בְּפוֹעַל
which is likewise the completeness of union in actual practice:
that one's whole body be surrounded
to take shelter in the shade of faith.
through the special virtue of the souls of Israel,
attachment to Hashem Yisbarach in essence,
"And you who cleave to Hashem your God,"
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קג, א)
and as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 103a)
"Every native in Israel shall dwell in sukkos":
"Whoever is of the stock and root of Israel
sits beneath the shade of faith."
